requirement: Derive separate subkeys for encryption, MAC and session use from one master key with HKDF-SHA256, binding each to its purpose and a version through the info string and validating key and output sizes.
skeleton: A PURPOSES frozenset, derive_subkey validating master length, purpose and output length before running HKDF with a versioned info string, and derive_all mapping every purpose to its subkey.
caption: Per-purpose key derivation with HKDF from the cryptography library. PURPOSES is the frozenset encryption, mac and session. derive_subkey(master, purpose, *, salt, length=32) raises ValueError saying the master key must be at least 32 bytes, ValueError naming an unknown purpose by repr, and ValueError saying the length must be between 16 and 64 bytes, both ends inclusive. It then runs HKDF with hashes.SHA256, the requested length, the given salt and info b'app/v1/' plus the purpose, and returns derive(master), so every purpose gets an independent key and changing the salt changes them all. derive_all(master, salt) returns a dict of the default 32 byte subkey for every purpose. The fixture asserts, against its own RFC 5869 HMAC-SHA256 reference, that each purpose's 32 byte key and the 48 byte mac key match exactly, that derive_all has the three purposes with distinct 32 byte keys, that salts a and b give different keys, that signing raises ValueError as an unknown purpose, that a 20 byte master raises ValueError, and that lengths 15 and 65 raise ValueError while 16 and 64 work.

plan.intent: Use one master secret for several cryptographic jobs safely
constraints: Subkeys come from HKDF-SHA256 with the salt and info app/v1/<purpose>
Each purpose yields a different key and the default length is 32 bytes
Master keys under 32 bytes raise ValueError
Lengths outside 16 to 64 inclusive raise ValueError

rationale.teaches: Put the purpose and a version in HKDF's info so one master key yields unrelated subkeys, and keep the salt in the derivation.
rationale.why: Reusing one key for encryption and MAC, or deriving without distinct info, couples the jobs so a weakness in one leaks into the other.

ops.docstring: Derive independent per-purpose subkeys from one master key with HKDF-SHA256.

candidates.why_wrong: The info string lacks the app/v1/ prefix, so keys differ from the versioned derivation.
Any purpose string is accepted, so typos silently derive new keys.
Master keys of 16 to 31 bytes are accepted although too short.
Subkeys default to 16 bytes instead of 32.
The salt is dropped from the derivation, so every salt yields the same keys.
